chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'May Allah improve you: A man divorced his wife while she was in a state of purity, without sexual intercourse, with the testimony of two just witnesses.' He said, 'When she enters the third menstruation, her waiting period is completed and she becomes permissible for marriage.'

I said to him, 'May Allah improve you: The people of Iraq narrate from Ali (peace be upon him) that he said: He has more right to take her back as long as she has not performed the ritual bath from the third menstruation.' He said, 'They lie.'

key_terms.رَجْعَة: Right to take back (in divorce context)

ai.seo_question: When does the waiting period end for a woman divorced before consummation according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific conditions for the completion of the 'Iddah' in a 'Taliq' (divorce before consummation) scenario, asserting that the period concludes with the third menstruation itself. He explicitly refutes the Iraqi school of thought, which held that the husband retains the right of revocation (Raj'a) until the woman performs the ritual bath (Ghusl) following that third period. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the physical event of menstruation as the definitive marker for the end of the waiting period, rather than the subsequent purification ritual.
